segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Hi Dana, thanks for making time. I wanted to walk through the updated quote for 42 seats and make sure the May 15 go-live still works on your side.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Yeah, that still works. We have 38 active users today, and I asked for 42 so we have a little room for the operations team in June.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Makes sense. The annual subscription comes to $31,080 before tax, and implementation is a one-time $4,500. That includes the admin training and the import of your last 18 months of data.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Okay. On billing, can you split the invoice between the subscription and implementation? Our finance team codes those separately.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yes, we can do two line items on one invoice, or two separate invoices if that is cleaner.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: One invoice is fine as long as the line items are separated. Payment terms are net 30, right?

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Correct, net 30. The subscription term would run May 15, 2026 through May 14, 2027, with renewal notice 45 days before the end date.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Good. The only other thing is the service language. Our legal team asked that the support response time be listed as one business day for standard issues.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yep, that is already in the order form under support terms. Critical issues are four business hours, standard is one business day.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Great. Send the final order form to me and copy Marisol in procurement. If it matches what we discussed, I can get signature by Friday.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Will do. I’ll send it this afternoon with the quote, order form, and the implementation summary attached.
